1. **Chart type**: Line chart with two series.

2. **Layout techniques**:  
- Single-panel chart  
- No faceting or small multiples  
- Multiple lines overlaid in the same coordinate system  
- Series distinguished by color and legend

3. **Data variables**:

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Year | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Annual change in population (millions of people) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis |
| Category (Immigration, Natural Increase) | Categorical/nominal | Line color/hue; legend |

Visible text elements:
- Title: **Annual Change in Population by Category**
- Y-axis scale shown in **millions of people**
- Legend categories: **Immigration** and **Natural Increase**

I notice that immigration and natural increase are declining as the years go by. Populations gain individuals through births and immigration. They lose individuals through deaths and emigration. These factors together determine how fast a population grows. 

I wonder if there is a significant decrease because in the years 2020 to 2021 because of the pandemic. Another factor is that people may be immigrating because of raises in taxes and supplies. I wonder if the population in 2017 and 2019 was decreasing of less immigration and a decline in fertility rates. Environmental factors can also be the leading cause since natural disasters are becoming stronger. 

Population decrease may have negative impacts on our community by declining innovations since immigrants make up most of the U.S and benefit other counties. Immigration  increases the economic output by increasing the size of the labor force. There is diversity with immigrants bringing their culture and ideas without them the world be dull. However, a positive impact of population decrease is a decrease in taxes because with an overgrowth of the population there is more mouth feed, properties to build, and more. 

"Take A Pledge to Contol the Population"

comments.raw_comment:
Welcome to Wednesday's live moderation of “What’s Going On in This Graph?”  

Today’s graph shows the components of total population change – net immigration (international in-migrants minus out-migrants) and natural population change (births minus deaths).  There was a mere 0.1 percent increase in the U.S. population in 2021, the slowest population growth in U.S. history.  

From 9 am – 2 pm E.T. today, share with us your responses online to these three questions -- "What do you notice?",  "What do you wonder?"  and “How will this affect you?”  Plus, please share with us a catchy headline that captures the ideas in this graph. 

By Friday morning, we’ll reveal the article that included this graph and much more.  We look forward to reading your discoveries.

Note that you can get a link to your response (and replies made to it) to share with your teacher and classmates by clicking the response box below your response “Email me when my comment is published.”  

Please visit our archive to see all graphs in this series (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphs).
View our archives that link to all past releases, organized by topic (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTopicIndex), 
graph type (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTypeIndex) and 
Stat Nugget (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsStatNuggetsIndex).  

The next “What’s Going On In This Graph?” will be released by Friday, April 22 with moderation on Wednesday, March 30.  The topic – free speech and cancel culture.  Keep noticing and wondering.
